text:
maria.c: quick ask — can someone run a short, reproducible compare across A100 / H100 / L40S for a longctx workload?
We need p50/p95/p99 token latency, throughput (tokens/s), gpu util, nvlink bytes, and a tiny kernel+driver note.
Target model: open-llm-7b (use same weights across runs). Sequence: 16k context, prompt 128 tokens, generate ~8k tokens.
Configs to test: batch=1 and batch=4; quant: fp16 and int8 (if available). Kernel/driver pinned in metadata.
Output: upload raw traces + bench CSV to s3://redwood-ci/bench/1765439876/{platform}/ and post the job id here. Need results by EOD tomorrow.

akshay: I can take this tonight. Will pin driver+cuda stack and PyTorch/torch-inductor versions.
What exact driver to pin? also do you want `continuous-batch` enabled?

maria.c: pin driver 535.104 (we saw weird fallbacks on older drivers). PyTorch 2.2 build with cu113/12 ok, but match what you use for prior H100 runs. Yes enable continuous-batch for batch=4 runs, and add a run with batching disabled as baseline.

akshay: got it. I'll run baseline (no CB), CB batch=4, and re-run for int8. Owner: @akshay.
Command i'm going to use (feel free to tweak):
```
run_bench --model open-llm-7b --devices $PLATFORM 
  --seq_len 16000 --prompt_len 128 --gen_len 8192 
  --batch 1 --batch 4 --continuous_batch true 
  --quant fp16 int8 
  --driver 535.104 --torch 2.2.0 
  --collect nvlink,gpu_util,allocator_traces 
  --out s3://redwood-ci/bench/1765439876/$PLATFORM/
```

bench-bot: job scheduled: RB-2026-1765439876-A (A100), RB-2026-1765439876-H (H100), RB-2026-1765439876-L (L40S). ETA 6h. Uploads will be automatic.

taylor: quick note — L40S int8 paths might choose different fused kernels. If you see perf delta >15% vs A100/H100 on int8, add a run with `--kernel-fallback true` so we can see the fallback cost.

leo: also capture `nvlink_bw` and `dram_bw` counters. For longctx this is often the tell. Use `--perf-counters nvlink_tx,nvlink_rx,dram_read_bytes,dram_write_bytes`.

akshay: will include perf counters. One question: do we need wallclock p99 across request-level bursts or the token-level p99?

maria.c: both. Token-level p99 and request-level p99 (end-to-end gen latency). Mark them in CSV columns `token_pXX` and `req_pXX`. Thanks.

akshay: logging path set. I'll also save `kv-cache-hit` traces to help explain microburst p99s.

sre-bot: FYI — if any run on H100 uses driver > 536 we need an infra change request. Confirm before switching.

akshay: noted. sticking to 535.104 for safety.

taylor: pinging @maria.c — do you want the diff report as raw CSV + jupyter or a summarized markdown PR?

maria.c: raw CSV + a 1-page markdown summary with top 3 takeaways (latency deltas, any nvlink bottlenecks, and recommended follow-ups). If there's a clear regression on H100 vs A100 for fp16/no-quant, call it out.

leo: small PS — if you run into OOM on L40S with int8 + batch4, reduce gen_len to 4k just for that config and annotate it.

akshay: understood. Starting runs now. I'll post RB job ids and S3 links when done.

bench-bot: RB-2026-1765439876-A: running -> 14% complete.

maria.c: thanks team — ping here if anything blocks. :thumbsup:

akshay: quick update at 2h: A100 baseline done, H100 baseline started. A100 fp16 batch1 p99 looks clean. Uploading CSV now. s3://redwood-ci/bench/1765439876/A100/baseline.csv

leo: nice. can you also snapshot `dmesg` + `nvidia-smi topo -m` for each node? helps rule out topology issues.

akshay: added those to the upload dir.

maria.c: perfect. will review once uploads finish.

bench-bot: all jobs completed. uploads: 
- s3://redwood-ci/bench/1765439876/A100/
- s3://redwood-ci/bench/1765439876/H100/
- s3://redwood-ci/bench/1765439876/L40S/

akshay: done. Summary coming in a PR in ~30m.

maria.c: excellent — thanks for the fast turnaround.

taylor: once PR is up, I'll do a quick kernel-level diff to see if L40S had fallback kernels on int8.

leo: and I'll run the perf counter aggregation script to produce stacked nvlink/dram graphs.

maria.c: closing the loop after PR. If anything surprising: we may schedule a deeper sweep with more seeds and longer runs.
